The finding correctly identifies that the light-theme value changed from 70% lightness to 30% lightness, which would significantly darken the text in light themes. This is inconsistent with other similar changes in the diff where the light-theme value typically preserves the original percentage (e.g., 50% stays 50%, 75% stays 75%). This appears to be an error where the percentages should likely be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))` to maintain the original light-theme appearance while adding dark-theme support.

adjudication_records.issue_text: app/assets/stylesheets/mobile/topic-post.scss:182 — Confidence 100, severity P2: `color: dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%));` changes the light-theme topic-link heading from the pre-change 20% to 50%, so rendering that mobile panel under a light theme alters heading emphasis outside the stated intent; the counterargument that matching 50% values is more consistent fails because consistency work was not requested, and restoring the first argument to 20% deletes the unrelated behavior change without touching dark themes.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows at line 179 (mobile/topic-post.scss) the h3 color changed from `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)` to `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. The finding correctly identifies that the first argument (light theme) changed from 20% lightness to 50% lightness, which is a behavioral change for light themes beyond just adding dark theme support. This appears to be an unintended side effect - the PR's purpose was to add dark theme support, not to change light theme appearance. The fix would be to use 20% in the first argument to preserve light theme behavior.
